checks: Diffed scripts/q39_q22.py against q36_q22.py: drop1 keeps only data rows 0-4 (removes the HCN/HCO+ 1-0 ratio and the two 3-2/1-0 rows), the chi2 sum honours the mask, ndat is reduced by 6, inf30 sets sigma=30% on rows 5-7. This matches the stated method. Agree.

Re-read out/q39/q39_post.log and q39_summary.csv: P(Te>=50) 0.45/0.46 baseline -> 0.37/0.40 drop1 -> 0.36/0.38 inf30 (cmb/nominal), as in the report. A shift of about -0.08 with sem 0.05 per configuration (difference sem ~0.07) is not significant, so 'not driven by 1-0' is supported. The claim is correctly worded as 'hot allowed, not required'.

N core: pooled median Tc_N 23.8 -> 14.2 K (cmb) and 24.7 -> 15.3 K (nominal) is real, and the per-seed scatter is stated (baseline sd 15-19 K). The S core is unchanged. The ln Z values are correctly flagged as not comparable because the data sets differ. Agree.

IR pumping: q39_irgrid.py is a reasonable first-order model (A(14um)=1.7/s, Honl-London splitting, v=0 collision rates copied to v2=1, a hard cut at N(v2=1)/N(v=0)>0.07 tied to Q4c). T_IR<=100 K has no effect. T_IR=150 K with W>=0.3 and T_IR=200 K are disfavoured (dlnZ -4 to -10, chi2 +8 to +19) and would lower P to 0.02-0.19. Report and log agree. The caveats are acknowledged: IR is applied to HCN in the cores only, with no HCO+ 12 um or envelope pumping, and W and T_IR are free.
notes_for_questioner: (1) The N-core Tc depends on the 1-0 data (N-S contrast Tc_N<=Tc_S without them). Ask for an independent N-core temperature tracer (CH3CN/HC3N/H13CN, vibrational lines) or a Band 3 matched-beam 1-0 test. (2) The per-seed scatter of P (0.2) is comparable to the effects tested, so the posterior is probably multimodal. A cheap robustness test is more SMC particles or nested sampling on the baseline N core. (3) The IR-pumping exclusion rests on copied collision rates and a free W, so state it as model-dependent in the post. Extend the test to HCO+ (12 um) if it is reused.
